result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both slides use the same layout: a headline that states the result, a two-bar chart of 412 vs 96, and a numbered list of the three changes, with no made-up monthly data. B puts the 412 and 96 figures in the headline itself, has cleaner spacing, and keeps the footer well apart from the content. A's bottom list rule nearly runs into the footer, and its large list text competes with the numbers. B's flaws are minor: the 412 label sits close to the headline, and it adds a derived −316 badge. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both slides use almost the same layout: a two-bar before/after chart with the three changes listed on the right. A puts 'from 412 to 96' right in the headline and has cleaner spacing at the bottom, though its '412' label sits close under the headline and the '−316 tickets' chip, while correctly calculated, adds something extra to look at. B leaves the numbers out of the headline, moving them to a smaller subtitle, and squeezes the footer against the list's bottom border, so it looks less finished.
